name: Nile Rodgers
hook: Chic's guitarist and co-writer, whose 'Good Times' became the first hit rap record's backing track and who then produced Bowie and Madonna's biggest records.

blurb.age13: Nile Rodgers was born in New York in 1952. With the bass player Bernard Edwards he formed Chic in 1977, a disco band known for tight, choppy rhythm guitar and melodic bass. In 1979 the Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight' was built on Chic's 'Good Times' without asking, and Rodgers and Edwards got their names added to the credits. Rodgers went on to produce David Bowie's 'Let's Dance' (1983) and Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' (1984), and in 2013 played on Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.
blurb.adult: Born on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in 1952. Chic, formed with Bernard Edwards in 1977 out of the Big Apple Band, made 'Le Freak' (1978), Atlantic's only triple-platinum single up to then, and 'Good Times' (1979). The Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight' interpolated 'Good Times' without permission; Rodgers and Edwards threatened action and were credited as co-writers, which Rodgers has called the one time he objected to his work being used. His production of Bowie's 'Let's Dance' and Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' carried the Chic rhythm section's approach into 1980s pop.
